gloss: table card; face-up card on the playing field

definitions.gloss: table card; face-up card on the playing field
definitions.explanation: A card that has been played and is lying face-up on the table in a card game. Used in hanafuda, karuta, and other traditional Japanese card games, as well as modern card games.

examples.japanese: {場札|ばふだ}を{確認|かくにん}してから{手札|てふだ}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Check the table cards before playing a card from your hand.

examples.japanese: {場札|ばふだ}に{合|あ}う{札|ふだ}が{手元|てもと}にない。
examples.english: I don't have a card in my hand that matches any of the table cards.

examples.japanese: {花札|はなふだ}では、{場札|ばふだ}と{同|おな}じ{月|つき}の{札|ふだ}を{手札|てふだ}から{出|だ}して{合|あ}わせると、{両方|りょうほう}を{取|と}ることができる。
examples.english: In hanafuda, if you play a card from your hand that matches the month of a table card, you can take both.

notes:
Composed of {場|ば} (place, field) and {札|ふだ} (card, tag). A card game term referring to cards that are in play on the table, as opposed to {手札|てふだ} (cards in one's hand) or {山札|やまふだ} (draw pile). Most commonly associated with {花札|はなふだ} (hanafuda) and かるた (karuta) but also used in other card games.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {場札|ばふだ}に{合|あ}わせる: to match a table card
- {場札|ばふだ}を{取|と}る: to take a table card
- {場札|ばふだ}を{並|なら}べる: to lay out the table cards

RELATED WORDS:
- {手札|てふだ}: hand (cards held by a player)
- {山札|やまふだ}: draw pile / stock pile
- {花札|はなふだ}: hanafuda — traditional Japanese flower card game
